text_fidelity_a:
Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment This calf raise machine is a great value piece of equipment for any home gym, on a budget. It's fairly comfortable, and allows you to easily do seated calf raises, and standing if you want to improvise a little bit. The big selling point is price, since many weight loaded seated calf machines are much more expensive for such a relatively simple movement. A big upside is there is pretty decent options for size adjustment to fit most people's needs.

The downsides are probably what allow the cost to be so low. While QC isn't necessarily bad, many pieces are not 'tight fitting', and need additional washers/spacers to make for a snug fit. Some pieces also needed to be manually widened so others would fit. Mechanically, this is a simplified seat calf machine, and takes several shortcuts in design that hurt QOL, such as the seat is mounted on the fulcrum, so you move as you perform the calf raise, and the handle to mount/unmount the machine from rest is on the rest-bar itself, in front of your knees, making it a little awkward to get in/out of. These are not deal breakers, but if you're used to 'gym-quality' equipment, this is does not meet the standard. However! it's so cheap that it doesn't even matter. Still get nasty calf pumps with this machine, 10/10 would buy again, as long as the price is cheap ~150$.
text_fidelity_b: Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment

text_fidelity_a:
NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako Got this to mount a MiNewt 150 on my helmet, and it's working well so far. It's kind of a tie-down thing with some pipe-insulation-like rubber under the plastic foot/pedestal to keep it from sliding around on the helmet. I've had it for about 2-3 weeks, so I can't comment on durability, but it has the same quick-release setup as the handlebar mount packaged with the 150. It tilts front and back, though not side-to-side. I'm using it with a Bell road helmet, and had no problems mounting it right in the center--as long as you have symmetrical vents in your helmet, you should be ok.

Good Stuff
With the right adjustments, you can get a good view of what's (well) ahead of you, and having it helmet-mounted allows you to pan and sweep the road ahead for pointy stuff and potholes. I also use it to alert drivers when approaching intersections--a quick look left and right gives a flash in their direction to get attention. The on-helmet setup seems to allow for longer "reach" from the light as well. One added bonus--drivers of high-profile vehicles (monster trucks, etc.) are more likely to see you since the light is well above the handlebars.

Notes and Concerns
If going for long rides in the dark, I'd recommend keeping a small blinky on the handlebars to complement the helmet mount (if you're not looking straight-ahead, your light isn't either). The mount is also made mainly of plastic--not sure what that does for long-term durability--may want to take it off if not doing night/dark rides, to minimize UV damage in the sun, etc. The mount does make the light sit rather high on the head, so it's not going to improve your aerodynamics or get you any style points (like a Roman centurion helmet profile), and it of course adds a bit of weight to the helmet.

Overall
I'd recommend this, especially for anyone who rides in the dark frequently or for long periods of time.
text_fidelity_b: NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako

text_fidelity_a:
POWERBLOCK Sport 24 I bought these in December 2019 and was very grateful to have them. Now it's December 2021, and I'm still working out at home with these as a key component of my strength training.

PowerBlocks can't compete with a full set of dumbbells like you get at commercial gyms, but they cover all of the major points that I need them to. Having my hands in a sort of box felt weird at first, but eventually I got used to it and can do most exercises as easily as I can with regular dumbbells. There are certain exceptions, like goblet squats. It's not that these moves are impossible, just extremely awkward. But this represents a very limited number of exercises.

There is a bit of rattle when the PowerBlocks are in motion, though they are secure. I don't think the rattle would be loud enough to disturb someone sleeping in another room with the door shut, though of course this is a subjective thing. When I compare it to the noise I'd make working with regular dumbbells, I'd say there's somewhat more because of the rattle (at least on fast move) but not at a high level.

Adjusting the weights is very simple and fast, but it is possible to misalign the adjuster so that it overlaps two weights rather than firmly latching onto one. This is easy to spot if you're paying attention, but note that it is possible to lift the weight when the adjuster is improperly set. I've done this a few times when in a hurry. At that point it's just a matter of setting the weight down and resetting the adjuster, but that's not something you'd want to be doing habitually for safety reasons.

After two years of use, the colored plastic bands on the tiers of weights are starting to get brittle and crack, but I'm not bothered by this. Actually, I'm surprised that these are holding up as well as they are given the humidity of my environment. More importantly, the metal is still in good shape and looks like it will continue to hold up for a long time to come.

With the weight levels properly set, the PowerBlocks are very stable and safe to use. I still wish this pair came out to 50 lbs rather than 48, but I think this is just how it is given the nature of the design. I'm lucky that I bought these before COVID hit, and I've certainly got my money's worth out of them.
text_fidelity_b: POWERBLOCK Sport 24

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall Our family does a lot of camping due to the boys and myself being in a scouting organization and enjoying the outdoors. I have been camping since I was a kid and have slept in numerous sleeping bags and have owned numerous coleman sleeping bags. I bought this Coleman White Water Large Cool-Weather Scoop Sleeping Bag from Amazon when it was a lightning deal back in November 2015. I have used the bag solely on our camp-outs since then. I have slept in it over a dozen nights under the stars in different temperature and weather conditions. Majority of the nights have been clear and low humidity with temperatures between 35-65 degrees.

This bag could sleep one and a half people (me and one of my kids) or one large person hence the name “large” in the title. In the description on Amazon says the bag is designed for 30-50 degree weather. We spent one weekend under the stars in the lower to mid 30s and it was cold and needed another blanket, however other nights between 40-60 degrees it is very comfortable.

So I would rate this sleeping bag 40 degrees and above. We do live in Georgia and humidity is high even in the winter time so in another climate 30 degrees may be comfortable in this bag. I liked that it is very comfortable sleeping on the ground with one of the most comfortable interiors of any sleeping bag i have slept in. The sleeping bag is made of 100% Polyester with 100% cotton fill. Overall a great deal if you can find it on sale.

Positives:
+Oversized for comfort
+Zipper does not get stuck in the material
+Comfortable (40-60 degrees)
+Five year warranty on stitching and workmanship

Negatives:
-Is not comfortable low to mid 30s
-Does not come with storage bag
text_fidelity_b: Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall

text_fidelity_a:
Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote This is a comfortable back pack.
The selling point for me was that it was listed to be able to accept an additional water bladder. And for me, (I hike in the Phoenix, AZ area mountains during the midday summer heat) that is important. Two 3liter bladders are a standard for me. Normally, I have to move up to my 35 litter backpack during the summer because the straps on my other packs are too narrow to adequately support the weight of two 3liter bladders (6 kilos or about 13lbs) in addition to my emergency first aid supplies, food, phone, and anything else I have. In total, about 25lbs (a little more than 11 kilos).

So it was a pleasant surprise that the straps on this 20 liter pack were almost as wide as the straps on my 35 liter pack. Making this pack easily able to comfortably carry the weight.

Also the waist belt has molle webbing for attaching additional things. For me, that's a phone carrier on one side and a 4x6 pouch on the other for some trail snacks (if I need the nourishment on the trail). A big plus. I don't have to remove the backpack to have a snack or to put the empty wrapper back in the pouch.
The waist belt also helps keep everything stable when I am trail running (probably about half of my normal 10 mile hike is trail running)

The padding on this backpack is much better than any of my other backpacks regardless of size. (I have 3l,6l,12l,18l,20l,25l,30l, and 35l backpacks.) Yes, I have a lot because I've never been able to find a nearly perfect fit for my needs, until now.

The bladder - this is a high quality bladder. (I now have four of them.) It has a nice high water flow. I'm easily drinking more during my hike because of this high flow rate. With my other bladders, I averaged about 1 liter an hour consumption. With these bladders, I average 1.5 liters an hour consumption. I have my garmin watch set to give a reminder every 8 minutes to drink water. So with the old bladders and the new Source bladders, I was drinking at the same intervals, it's just easier to drink through the Source drinking tube than the other ones resulting in the higher consumption.

Strap management - this thing has elastic on each of the straps to hold the excess strapping. Wow, so nice. No Irish pennants (marine corps terminology referring to the the stray threads sticking out on clothing) flying all over the place

I do have one complaint though, it says that it'll accept a second bladder. But there's only the one strap in the water bladder compartment to hold a bladder. To accommodate a second bladder, you have to place it in the main storage compartment. But there is no strap to hold a bladder there. And you have farther to run the tube for this second bladder. I started keeping some storage at the bottom of the main compartment (sun block, towels, etc.) that manages to raise up the second bladder so that the drinking tube for that bladder isn't uncomfortably short to drink through. Otherwise the second bladder sits low enough that the tube is a little short (perhaps about 5 or 6 inches shorter than the tube for the water bladder in the water bladder compartment).
text_fidelity_b: Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote

POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel I am rating two stars because it does NOT perform as promised in an important area AND because the company never responded to my request for support.

First, I'm an experienced swimmer; I'm 60+ but I can still swim a mile in under 30 mins and complete a 200 IM, so it's not like I don't know what I'm doing in the water. I've tried and tried -- and really tried -- to love this.

Pluses: SWIMMING with the Powerbreather is a breeze, and I actually enjoy the stress it places on my lungs, forcing me to breathe deeply. When I am swimming point to point I can work on my stroke, don't have to gasp to breathe, etc.

Negative: But doing flip turns is a nightmare! No matter what configuration I try, when I flip the tube fills w/ water and, because it is LITERALLY screwed onto the head, I have to race to release it before I am breathing water. Choking, gasping... this is not my idea of a good time. I've re-read all the literature, and everything points to my being able to do flip turns, which is specifically why I purchase the most expensive version, the Wave. I've reviewed all their pictures and videos, and notice that NOWHERE do they demonstrate anyone doing a flip turn using the device. Interesting. I've written to their customer service on their website asking for help and complaining I can't complete a flip turn w/o taking on water and is there any help they can offer and... crickets. Nothing.

I even had a swimming buddy try out the unit, thinking that "maybe it's me... maybe my flip turns are off." Nope, he took on water, as well.

I am keeping this because I do enjoy open water and ocean swimming, and occasionally it's useful to work on my stroke in the pool, as long as I'm OK doing clumsy top-of-water turns at either end of the pool. But I am terribly disappointed I cannot actually work out in a pool using the breather.
text_fidelity_b: POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel

text_fidelity_a:
Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer As there are plenty of reviews, I'm going to do a review that assumes you've read the rest and I will try and hit some of the criticisms. I've owned my DMT for about a month and a half. I'm not an overly picky or difficult person, as some reviewers seem to be. Not criticizing them, just letting you know that I may be easier going than you are. I got mine at $2399 so for me this was a bit of an investment and I read all the reviews I could find. Since Smooth only seems to publish the great reviews on their website, I am publishing mine here. I do think the Treadmill Doctor reviews are fair and accurate, but they seem to have a chummy relationship with Smooth.

I ordered the unit and the Smooth Sync Bluetooth module. I ordered it with the white glove service as I'm lazy and it's heavy. First, the ordering process, here is my timeline:

- 12 Jan 13, Order placed with Smooth via web
- 12 Jan 13, Email confirmation of order
- 18 Jan 13, Credit card charged
- 18 Jan 13 Product Shipped Notice
- 27 Jan 13, Contacted by shipping/assembly company
- 28 Jan 13, Product received/assembled
- 29 Jan 13, Smooth Sync received/installed

The unit arrived in one large box and one ridiculously large box. It would have been difficult for my 21 year-old son and I to get it in the house. Unless you are awfully burly or have moving equipment (a standard dolly won't get it) then at least have it delivered to the room where you want to set it up. When assembled, even using the wheels, if I moved it by myself I would be hurting the next day. As others have said, the assembly duo (from CEVA Logistics) had never seen one before, but had assembled similar items. They assembled it correctly without damage to the unit or anything else in about an hour. I'm pretty handy and I think I could have done it a bit quicker. If you assemble it yourself, you are primarily assembling the upright portion. When we tried using it the first time, something was banging. They disassembled one section, reassembled and everything was grand.

Smooth forgot to ship the Smooth Sync so it wasn't available day one, but UPS ground got it here the next day. It installed in just a few minutes with no problems.

I did quite a bit of research before buying. I use ellipticals at the gym and I own a top of the line Bowflex. The Agile DMT replaced a Proform 7.0 Treadmill that gave up the ghost after 14 years and several moves. In terms of engineering, construction and features, there is absolutely no comparison between this and my Proform. This is a gym quality machine with more features than any gym will ever pay for. Contrary to what others have said, the speakers are not bad. The fan is a bit cheap, but on the highest setting it provides a little breeze. The display/control panel is functional but not impressive.

Others commented on all the plastic. While it seems a little silly, it does cover a lot of the moving parts such that you can move around the device without hooking or snagging and it prevents dust and dirt and will make it easier to clean.

As I mentioned, I bought the Smooth Sync. While $130 seems like a lot, if you consider that you are paying for the hardware, the app and the integration, it is not bad. The MySmooth app is good. The video application is interesting, but definitely not something I would pay $20 a video for. It appears Smooth spent quite a lot to shoot the videos. In the current market, they would probably be better off letting users upload their own with the MySmooth app controlling the speed of play. The Android app does not record workouts and accessing the History button crashes the application. Smooth does not have a page with news about the app.

As for customer service, I've never received any response from Smooth that appeared remotely human. It took 6 days to get another email after I placed my order. When the CEVA tracking showed that my machine had been in town for a week and I had received no call, I sent an email to Smooth. I got no reply, but I noted on the bill of lading that Smooth had contacted CEVA and told them to get moving. CEVA called me the day after I sent the email (email Saturday, call Sunday, delivery Monday). When I sent Smooth an email to ask about my Smooth Sync (several weeks after I ordered it) my response was the UPS email notice with no other response. The device arrived the next day via UPS ground. In my book, this is adequate but certainly well below average. I would have expected the order confirmation to provide some type of information on when I could expect a follow-up on shipping. I would have expected them to ship my Smooth Sync so that it was here when the machine arrived. For the price, I would expect at least a follow-up email to see how the delivery/install went and if I had any problems. All of this would really merit a "very good" not an "exceptional" these days. I get follow-up emails from eBay sellers to see if I'm satisfied with a .99 cable.

Smooth was recently purchased. The new owner is continuing the product line and honoring all warranties, etc. Supposedly they are investing millions. Hopefully the person in charge of customer service takes his or her buyout and moves on to be replaced by someone more competent. I say that as I think the products are excellent, so it is too bad when one person brings the company down to simply being good.

As for the white glove delivery install, I live in the DC area. If you don't get experienced assembly people here, odds are you won't elsewhere. My installers got it together with no problems and didn't take all day. I'm satisfied and would do it again.
text_fidelity_b: Smooth Fitness Agile DMT Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Wahoo BLUEHR Heart Rate Monitor for iPhone and Android This is my 3rd heart rate monitor (HRM). Not because they break, but because I got a better phone! Anyhow, I received this Wahoo BlueHR at about the same time I had gotten a [[ASIN:B007S088F4 Polar H7 Bluetooth Smart Heart Rate Sensor]] to use with my new iPhone 5. I preveiously was using a a Garmin HRM, which I still have, but it uses the ANT+ technology and I need an adapter on my iPhone in order to use. The bluetooth is nice because it pairs easily with the DigiFit app that I use. I can't speak for the Wahoo app, because I have not tried that as I've been using DigiFit with a lot of success since the beginning of the year and love that app so why change?

Anyhow, if I compare the Wahoo BlueHR with the Polar H7 they is not too much difference. They are about the same size and the strap is similar with the same fit. The one thing I do not like about both of them is the sensor part (or whatever it's called - the big transmitter-like piece that snaps on). It's not really that bad, but when I'm wearing it and doing some exercises that require me to lay on my chest (like on a bench or stability ball) the thing is not as comfortable as the old Garmin HRM [[ASIN:B000UOD5QM Garmin Heart-Rate Monitor]] which is flat all across the front. Honestly, it's not that big of a deal for the few times I do those types of workouts, but important to note.

the Wahoo HRM does seem to take a few seconds longer to sync up than the Polar when I first start my workouts, but once connected, I haven't lost signal for it. I've been using the Wahoo HRM for about 3 weeks now - have used it for weight lifting 3 days a week, running 2 days a week and bicycling 2 days a week. No problems at all and I love that I can keep track of my heart rate throughout my workouts. the DigiFit app even has some health assessments that I use to get custom heart rate zones based on a prescribed workout. I've run the Advanced Cardio assessment, the Cooper Running Test, and the Critical Power 30-minute (CP30) assessments to determine my heart rate training zones. (these are through the DigiFit app which guide you through them).

I did not experience any issues with this as others have stated, and hopefully the "dead out of the box" is not because they can't find it showing up in their bluetooth settings because with these devices you need to sync it within the app. I think it may have something to do with the Bluetooth 4.0 technology - because they only work with the smartphones/devices that support Bluetooth 4.0, also called Bluetooth Enhanced or BLE. does not work with the iPhone 3Gs - that much I know. There really is little documentation that comes with the device and there really should be something to make it clear that it needs to be paired through an app if you're using it with a smartphone.

oh, and I also have the Wahoo Speed & Cadence sensor on my bike which works great as well.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo BLUEHR Heart Rate Monitor for iPhone and Android

Smith & Wesson Extraction and Evasion SW671 15.9in Full Tang Tomahawk with a 3.9in Steel Blade and TPE Handle for Outdoor, Tactical, Survival and EDC For what it is, and for the price I paid, this is a sturdy and well-made full tang hawk that will blow through most things that get in its way. It is elegantly designed as a working tool to help get you out of tight spots. Being a one piece chunk of steel with a comfortable handle fastened to the shaft with four bolts, this is not a flimsy tool that will fly apart when confronted with heavy work. It is well-balanced and comfortable to hold with either one or two hands. It's also big enough to allow choking up if you need more control and a shorter stroke.

Its uses are virtually endless. Because of its solid construction and reasonable price, I wouldn't hesitate to use it in any situation. The chances of this breaking are slim and even if it does, you're only out about $30.00. Very few tomohawk makers have a straight spike on the opposite end of the blade. There are a few situations that I can think of where you would use the spike but would have to rapidly pull it out before striking again. It won't do you any good to kill a zombie and have your hawk stuck in its skull. Of course that would only happen with a fresh one, an older model will be brittle and your spike should blow right through it.

This hawk came sharp but didn't pass the paper test. A little extra elbow grease and that can be rectified. It's weight might be a little restrictive for people without much arm strength and it might be a bear to carry all day if hiking. The sheath that comes with it will cover the axe head and ride on your belt. Just don't expect that to work too well for you. This ideally would be carried in your vehilcle and used when unexpected circumstances arise. Even if you don't know what you're doing with it, just holding it will inspire confidenc. And often times attitude can be the tipping point in getting any job done.

Solo Stove 2 Pot Set: Stainless Steel Companion Pot Set for Solo Stove Campfire. Great for Backpacking, Camping, Survival The Solo Stove Campfire and Solo Stove 2 Pot Set are the perfect companions!
Once again the makers have outdone themselves.

The Solo Stove Campfire in it's nylon bag nests perfectly inside the Solo Stove 2 Pot Set.
The stove and pots are both sturdily constructed of beautiful stainless steel.

The third and largest in the all stainless Solo Stove line, the Campfire is perfect for replacing it's namesake traditional "campfire".
This past weekend I had a cookout with friends we had the Campfire and my friend had a propane grill.

While my friends grill was heating up, we quickly got a roaring file going in the Campfire. It was easy to set up and get going.
I keep a set of Fiskars pruning shears on hand to easily prep my stove fuel into about 4 inch length peices from downed tree limbs.

Start off with some small tinder in the bottom then a squirt of alcohol hand sanitizer as an accelerant, set it off with a lighter.

Begin adding on processed twigs from thinnest to thickest. I would say it was only about 5 minutes for the fire to get big enough
for the gassification effect to kick in and the blazing fire was eating the thicker branch peices with ease.

On this cold day we all enjyed standing around the Campfire to stay warm.

The stainless pots heated up nicely and evenly as we boiled water for tea.
The pot was easy to remove from flame with fold out handles or the bail handle.

When you want a campfire without a campfire ring and campfire mess, this is the ticket.

Highest quality product, highly recommended with no reservations!

Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android This RFLKT+ bike computer worked great with my iPhone 5, especially once I figured out how to use it! the instructions are bad - as in they have a small piece of paper in the box that tells you to scan the code to get to the instructions. I understand the reasoning - "technology changes fast and we want you to have the most up to date instructions." Okay, but sadly the instructions did not match the version of the device that I had, so I had to figure out some of it on my own. I mean you'd think they would keep the online instructions up to date if that's the reason they want you to go online to get them. I would have appreciated a brief "quick start" paper instruction inside the box.

Okay, enough about the instructions. Once I figured it out, this little device collected flawless from my iphone although you need to keep the app active or else the device shuts down. think of it as an extension of your iphone screen - a second monitor. I also have a Garmin heart rate monitor (ANT+) and a Garmin speed/cadence sensor (ANT+) on my bike. the Wahoo found both of those quickly and displayed the data accurately. I matched it against my Garmin 310XT watch and it matched up perfectly.

The one thing I had to remember was to start the app on the phone in order to get the distance and time to start recording! I was cruising along and watching my heart rate and cadence but couldn't figure out why the mileage wasn't getting logged until I realized I hadn't started things up on the iPhone. So this works well, and if you've already got other apps and like using your iphone then this is a great little device.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android

text_fidelity_a:
Sportsroyals Stair Stepper with Resistance Band and Vertical Climber Exercise Machine for Home, More Than 300lbs Weight Capacity I had a stepper back in the 90s that I liked and used often, but it grew tight, hard to step (they tightened), and I ended up dumping it after only a few months. I wasn’t sure I’d ever get another stepper because of this, but as I’m trying to get in exercise even when I can’t always do the things I normally do. But would this be worth it - and why is with that “side to side” movement?

1. It arrives almost completely assembled, with only the handles needing to be hooked on and the readout box mounted.
2. The mounting of the box is easy - hook onto the attached cord, then place it onto the mount.
3. The handles are easily attached with carbeaner hooks.
4. You’re ready to go!
5. The platforms for your feet are large, wide, and should fit most foot/shoe sizes. There are “ridges or ripples” to the surface; they are not ‘hard,’ but rather produce a good traction surface. I am standing on them and did 100 steps in bare feet to see how comfortable and I was fine. Could have kept going. In shoes they are equally comfortable and keep my feet (with/without shoes) from slipping.
6. The handles and bungee are great for added effort. I’ll usually keep them in my hands throughout the workout, altering using/not using them, changing the direction I’m pulling in in order to give my arms various things to do. They provide a solid workout, giving my arms a nice burn to compliment the work my legs are going.
7. THE STEPPING... I was worried about the side to side movement of the stepping - I’ve never seen or experienced this before. I LOVE it! In the past I’ve had issues with my hips and knees from stepping - or treadmills - but I find this movement is very natural and for some reason does not cause me pain. I recently tore my hamstring, but I’ve hit a point in recovery where I’ve been on the stepper every day for a week and I’ve felt great - it’s actually worked some minor knee pain I’ve been having WHILE stepping. This is a great movement and I’m thrilled it’s part of the design.
8. So far the stepping is very smooth - I feel like the system used to create the movement is superior to the steppers I had in the 90s. This leads me to think it’ll last far longer than that stepper system. If it does, this will be a perfect unit for me.
9. It’s a great height, sturdy, and strong. Okay, it’s heavy - but it should be. It has to hold you up and in place - and it does. It’s height is nice - I can stand at my conversion standup/sit down desk and work. And it’s strong enough to make me feel safe and secure.

Overall this is a great unit and I’m thrilled with it. I’ve been at it a week and feel like it’s becoming a regular part of my workouts. I’m happy to recommend this stepper.
text_fidelity_b: Sportsroyals Stair Stepper with Resistance Band and Vertical Climber Exercise Machine for Home, More Than 300lbs Weight Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
NHL Sting Ray Air Powered Hockey Table - 84 Inch - Features Scratch Resistant Material, Automatic Scoring, and Complete with All Accessories Mostly this is excellent, but it could have been so much more!

Putting this together is easy enough, nicer to have two pairs of hands on the job, no problem with only one. Then you get to use it. Lets start with whats right.
You plug it in, pop up the score board, switch it all on and you are off! The sound effects really help, the fun is fast and furious, the game play is great. It senses goals well, had no false goals or missed ones - just perfect.

What really lets this down is the power. The line to an outlet has a little inline rotating switch (like you get on cheap light fittings) just hanging below the table so you have to scramble on the floor to start and stop the fan.
The gaming computer runs on batteries! The batteries go to a plug on the computer! How stupid is that?
There should be a toggle switch on the underside of the table. That should power the fan, AND a 3.5 v power pack for the computer. For the price, it is insane that it does not have this, and I would see that as a deal breaker. I dont want to have to get on my back, underneath the table, unscrewing the battery case and replacing the batteries once every few months. I am modifying mine to work of one simple switch. That is how it should have shipped.
text_fidelity_b: NHL Sting Ray Air Powered Hockey Table - 84 Inch - Features Scratch Resistant Material, Automatic Scoring, and Complete with All Accessories

At first, I wasn't sure about the inflation, but being inexperienced with this type of product, I really didn't know what to expect (would it inflate like an air mattress, or would inflation be minimal?). When I first unrolled it, it didn't seem to inflate, even after the 3-5 minutes described in the instructions. Then I realized I unrolled it with the valve closed, and the instructions state to unroll with the valve open. So, I rolled it back, squeezing out what air had entered it, then proceeded to unroll again with the valve open. After several minutes, I came back, put it on the floor and tested it. It had inflated significantly more (don't expect an air mattress), though still remained thin. For me it was fairly comfortable on its own, and with my sleeping bag on top of it, it was more than comfortable enough for camping.

After testing it for comfort on the hard floor in my house, I rolled it back up, and a lot of air came out. It was easy to roll and easily went back into its carry bag, which is a big plus (too many products never fit back in their original packaging).

So, short of knowing how it would do on the ground outside in cold weather, I'd say this product was worth the purchase. It seems to be made of high-quality material, and it provides added comfort for sleeping in a sleeping bag.
text_fidelity_b: Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot

text_fidelity_a:
Black Diamond Spot Headlamp My favorite low priced headlamp.
Not the quality of high tech wonder lamps. But there are no real faults. And the interface is very good.
All inputs on one button which is the best way to do it, fewer moving parts to go wrong.
3 inputs : momentary push, 3 second push, 6 second push.
If the lamp is on :
Momentary push cycles on/off.
Long push gradually dims the light in steps.
(when it reaches the dimmest it will flicker once to indicate lowest level,
then it gradually brightens the light, step at a time, flickers once on highest).
This works very well to set the brightness levels.

When light is OFF:
momentary push turns it on (two outer lights for flood, or center for spot. Repeat pushes will alternate: spot, off, flood, off, spot,...
3 second push : turns on the red lamp
6 second push: turns on the lock mode (locks lamp off until another 6 sec. push turns it back on. A blue light on the side will go on for a couple seconds to verify the lamp is locked).

I find the interface easy to use to get it to do as I like when I like.
5 different tilt settings from straight down to higher than straight forward. There are settings I find perfect for reading or watching your step on the trail. And they stay put.

Very bright on spot!
The flood is very spread out, lights up the whole room or tent.

5 stars.
------

Another lamp that costs about $10 more is the Princeton Tec EOS TACTICAL. The tactical model of the EOS line is military issue from several governments. Bulletproof and rugged, really waterproof. But the ergonomics are military rough: the button is very hard to push (so it won't wear out), the battery box takes a tool like a dime to open (so they could never fall out by mistake). A better choice if you going to climb mount Everest and your life depends on the lamp. Not as good as this BDSH for using in common outdoor camping, running, hunting, imo.

Those are the two under $50 that I like.

EDIT: I should have noted the reviews stating the tilt lock stops would fail. They failed in 6 months on one of mine of these. The other two I have are getting weaker and weaker (about a year old). Then the lamp just tilts all the way forward and points at your toes. No way to reset the tilt after the mechanism breaks. I changed my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars. I do NOT recommend these.
text_fidelity_b: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp

text_fidelity_a:
Case XX Sod Buster Jr. 00032 Knife This review is going to be biased. Can't be helped. My first three knives were a Barlow (a really cheap one) a Victorinox and a Case stockman (or was it a trapper) . Idk, my dad stole all of these from me when I got old enough to do any damage with them. The case is the only one I miss. I'm tempted, as a 40 year old grown man, to go rifling through his drawers to find it. And my pellet gun.
The Sodbuster is the biggest Case knife I've ever seen. My father-in-law carries a trapper and usually I got my Tx toothpick on me, but when I got this sucker, I was pretty impressed with its size. Let's get the obvious stuff out of the way, it's a slipjoint (a really easy one too), no pocket clip, no newfangled blade steel. It's a work knife for digging around in a garden. Some folks will be turned off by all of these things. I look at them as plusses. I'm not sure where the idea that a non-locking blade = dangerous came about. You really do have to handle slipjoints slightly differently than locking blades but they are just as safe if not safer in most contexts. It's a matter of exposure. I carved wood with my barlow for years, and occasionally the blade would stick or something but I always knew that could happen. I did have one close on my fingers once or twice but there wasn't any force behind it and not really anything happened as a result. I think most modern knife folks grew up with a slipjoint and maybe injured themselves with one as a kid, possibly while clowning around with it, to the point where as adults they think of them as an unnecessary hazard. The pocket clip... well I could take it or leave it. It's easier for a work knife not to have to fish around in my pocket for it repeatedly. That said, mostly I leave this one on my desk or table. Not sure I would carry it around in public. It's mighty big for a pocket. As for the blade steel, I generally prefer high carbon steel. I can sharpen such a knife really well with a stone. I'm not sure that I really like the edge retention of modern steels. I have an r2d2 - I have yet to sharpen it, but I'm guessing it will be a pain in the butt. I know exactly what to expect with softer steels.. In short, this is a fine knife appointed well for the last millenia. It's the folksier version of a RAT 1 and it will appeal to any who like the shape.
text_fidelity_b: Case XX Sod Buster Jr. 00032 Knife

XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination I received this light for my Dahon folding commuter bike. Previously I was using a small rechargeable light that was more for visibility to oncoming cars than to actually see the ground.

This extra illumination of this light has made a significant difference for me when commuting at night. I used to avoid areas with low illumination. The XOSS illuminates the ground in front like a car headlight allowing me to ride in total darkness. I tilt the light so can see everything coming at me from about 20-30 feet away, which is enough time to react at my normal riding speed.

I have also used both the automatic on/off motion sensor and standard on/off modes and they each worked well.

The handlebar attachment/removal system allows me to use the XOSS as a flashlight (have done this several times) and more easily charge it. However, the attachment clip has an issue - if you tighten it onto the handlebars too much, the screw will enter a hole on the bottom of the light and restrict it from being put on or removed. Topeak Mondo Pack with Fixer F25 with Extendable Back Pocket, 12.6 x 5.1 x 6.3-Inch (X-Large) A great product, certainly up to Topeak's standards. The pouch is huge and very roomy. It has a great side compartment to prevent your tools from beating up your snacks, and has a nice mesh pocket perfect for CO2 cartridges. Two caveats are worth considering. First, there is a temptation to stuff the main compartment full of stuff, and this is a great idea for a long ride. If you do so, it will require some unpacking to get to all of the gear, so pack the stuff you want to access quickly (e.g. food!) near the zipper. You can pack the tubes out of the way, if you blow one, you likely don't have a problem with the extra minute it takes you to get to it. The second issue to be aware of is that this pack is HUGE. Measure your bike to make sure that it fits, and make sure that you are happy with the look (it looks nothing like a wedge pack).

I was aware of both issues, and I love the pack! It lets me ride VERY long rides on my road bike without support and without a trunk bag.

It also had a lot of blade play (slop) which always makes me doubt the construction quality. I finally got seduced by a picture of a Benchmade Bedlam. It just plain looked wicked and I had to have it. Unfortunately it also lacked in quality.

Benchmade's fixed blade knives have always had a great reputation. I saw the Nimravus at a gun and knife show and was impressed by the weight and balance. It was solidly built in the mode of my Busse fixed blades. It is sinister looking, built like a tank with a very sharp tanto blade, and has the look of a weapon that would get my attention immediately if it were pulled on me. The overall size is almost perfect, it fits my hands well, the construction is robust, and it is extremely well-balanced.

Always remember to use extreme caution when handling knives. An old-timer once told me that they are just as dangerous as guns because they are always loaded. One slip can have disastrous results. So until you can go to Walmart and buy a new finger, or can print one with a 3D printer, be careful out there.
text_fidelity_b: Benchmade - Nimravus 141SBK Knife, Tanto Blade, Serrated Edge, Coated Finish, Black Handle, Made in the USA

Razor A5 Lux Kick Scooter for Kids Ages 8+ - 8" Urethane Wheels, Anodized Finish Featuring Bold Colors and Graphics, for Riders up to 220 lbs What I dislike?? I paid 67 last week now it is LESS....lol. But I will say it is worth the money. I am a 52 year old 5'10" adult and the last time I rode a Razor Brand kick scooter Harry Potter was in the theaters and I was "old" for scooters then. And had a very bad wreck due to the brake not really supporting my weight.
Rest assured ...I am under the 220 pound limit and the brake on this DOES work but not on a dime. Plan ahead.
The huge wheels make cracks and bumps easy. On smooth pavement it is a smooth ride....on rough pavement.....yep, rough ride. Will jar you pretty good. I use it for an 8 block radius. I have seen reviews of people who use it for much larger spans. I just WISH this product had existed when I was a teen or in my 20s. Also, if you meet a heel too steep to kick scoot, it is very easy to just pick it up or push it till you can easily go again. I think it weighs about 7 lbs. Don't quote me but that is something anyone can handle.

Here is what to know....as long as you an adult rider do not take this to a skate park, these days, no one is gonna laugh or poke fun. Scooters are hot now whether electric or kick and this scooter is great for people young or old. It is low to the ground, easy to kick, easy to ride, light weight...total fun.
I own the Razor E300. I wanted this for different reasons. It is 100 percent suitable for an adult human to ride. It IS a scooter and you could fall so wear your helmet. You already look a tad goofy....so don't worry what others think. Put that helmet to protect your brain and enjoy a fun ride!

text_fidelity_a: Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash – PS1543 - Stand up Paddle Board Hook-and-Loop System with Comfortable Neoprene Padding at Ankle My wife and I recently got a couple of inflatable SUPs to take out - we had done some SUP and kayak tours and wanted to go out on our own. To that end, we also decided to grab this Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash when I had the chance. The SUPs came with leashes, but I’d heard the Pelican brand was pretty good and one thing we experienced on the tours was rubbing from the leashes. We both have backgrounds as athletes, which also includes injuries and the like, and as we age, we find that comfort is as important to us as anything. And the rubbing we had experienced was enough to consider not even going out again. So... we wanted leashes that would feel good. This Pelican Boats -SUP Premium Unisex Ankle Leash feels very good. Now we haven’t been out on the water (our state requires flotation devices that we haven’t gotten yet, and weather has kept us off), but we put this (and another Pelican leash) through some tests here at home and come away feeling very positive. text_fidelity_a:
Rep Fitness Adjustable Bench – AB-3000 FID – Flat/Incline/Decline I spent a LOT of time researching benches (really, way too much time), but bottom line was that I wanted something stable, adjustable, and of course I didn't want to break the bank. There are a lot of really questionably pricey benches out there -- and when it comes down to it a bench is a very simple piece of equipment. Why are they so expensive? After all of my time investment I am confident in saying that absolutely no other bench on the market combines the features of this bench and its low price.

Specifics:

Delivery -- Typical, left outside of my house.

Packaging -- Decent. The inner boxes were a bit torn up as Rep didn't put enough padding in place. But none of the parts were damaged.

Instructions -- Complete joke. The "assembly" instructions are a single page parts diagram and then a second page of "tips." Come on, at least provide a step-by-step guide? Please visit any IKEA store to learn how it's done.

Assembly -- The instructions are not completely useless; everything can be figured out from the diagram. There is some mention of videos to be watched, but I couldn't be bothered. Overall it wasn't bad but it definitely took longer than the stated 15 minutes -- probably closer to 45.

The biggest issue for me was getting the seat bolted into place. The "tips" sheet shows it being done with the cushion up, which would require some extreme form of dexterity that I don't possess. After a while I realized that I could un-bolt the seat from the base of the unit (this requires removing a bolt that comes already in place from the factory) and then just flip the whole thing back -- after that the rest of the assembly was very simple.

Note that the bolts are a bit on the large side. Neither of my two ratchet sets had anything quite big enough (mine go up to 9/16"), so I had to use a combination of an adjustable wrench and the provided sheet metal "multitool." This undoubtedly slowed me way down.

Overall assembly includes screwing in maybe 8 bolts for the seat and back, two for the ankle pads, and then another four or so for the rest of the unit. Then you go through and tighten everything down, including the bolts that were put on at the factory.

Utilization -- Once assembled, the unit feels extremely sturdy. It sits perfectly on the floor without rocking, and gives me full confidence. The pads are plenty comfortable in my opinion; sure they're a bit stiff, but it's not like I'm going to take a nap on the thing. Also I suspect that these pads will hold up better over time than softer ones would.

Adjustment is simple for both the seat and the back and there are plenty of options for what I need to get done on a daily basis. One important note is that when flat or in decline there is definitely a considerable gap between the seat and back. I know this bothers a lot of people. I don't mind it and don't find it uncomfortable, but I do notice it; if you're looking for something gap-free, look elsewhere.

Not much else to say. I think despite the few flaws, for the price this bench is absolutely unbeatable and will serve me for many years. I'm very happy with my purchase...and I can use the money saved to buy more weights to test that 1,000 pound capacity limit!
text_fidelity_b: Rep Fitness Adjustable Bench – AB-3000 FID – Flat/Incline/Decline

text_fidelity_a:
Wurkkos DL30 Scuba Diving Flashlight - Scuba Dive Light Super Bright Max 3600 Lumen with 5000K 90CRI,100m Underwater Flashlight IPX-8 Waterproof Submersible Flashlight with USB Charger This flashlight is a bit heavier than others in this size range. I think that is leaning more toward the battery size. The 21700 battery weighs 2.5 ounces whereas the 18650 is 1.5 ounces. The flashlight without the 21700 battery weighs 4.9 ounces. Another thing is it gets very warm from holding it in your hand on high mode for 5 minutes. A few minutes longer and it gets HOT and almost hard to hold unless you are wearing gloves. With this said the flashlight is designed for diving and stays a lot cooler under water. I submerged it in cool water and the flashlight does not get more than warm on high mode. It is the 3 LEDs that cause all the heat.

I love the brightness and the ease of turning the switch on and off. The 3 brightness settings are a good feature in my opinion and work flawlessly. To show how bright the high setting is, I included a picture of our stove with kitchen light off and standing about 7 feet back and no camera flash. If you store the flashlight for long periods of time, or if traveling and want to make sure the flashlight doesn't accidently turn on, you can just turn the tail cap backwards less than 1 turn and the flashlight is totally off. It works, I tested it! Wonderful!! The lens is very solid and thick. It appears to be nearly indestructible. Another feature is this item comes with a cover adapter for using the smaller 18650 battery that is standard in most flashlights. The 18650 wouldn't have as long a running time but runs a little cooler using this flashlight above water. We tested a fully charged 18650 on high for 5 minutes and it drained the battery to 64 percent. It is also just a bit less bright but noticeable. Testing the 21700 battery fully charged for 5 minutes above water drained the battery to 87 percent and when putting it back to charge it finished to 100 percent in about 17 minutes. We used a MiBoxer 8 battery charger that shows percentages while charging. Amazon sells them and we love it.

This flashlight in my opinion really is best underwater use. I also think if it was used as a normal flashlight and running it for 15 minutes or more on high on a hot evening could burn out the LEDs from the heat. The manual does not mention this and it says the flashlight has a built in ATR (advanced temperature regulation) and will reduce the power under certain situations of excessive heat to prevent overheating.

If you just wanted to use it above water for shorter times to find something lost like your wife's wedding ring because she got mad at you, this little gem is excellent and fits into most any size pocket. But it is SO bright you really do NOT want to look into it, and also have to be careful not to shine it in anyone’s face, and that includes pets.

Overall this is a great flashlight and I recommend it for quality and value!
text_fidelity_b: Wurkkos DL30 Scuba Diving Flashlight - Scuba Dive Light Super Bright Max 3600 Lumen with 5000K 90CRI,100m Underwater Flashlight IPX-8 Waterproof Submersible Flashlight with USB Charger

TiTo High Strength Titanium Alloy Tent Stakes Tent pegs Nail pegs for Canopy Camping Tent Dia 8mm and Length 240mm only 56G (8x300mm) These are the beefiest, most heavy duty titanium tent stakes I've ever seen. It is kind of overkill, making these out of titanium when a good chromoly steel of the same weight would be nearly as good. I'm sure a company could make quality steel stakes (albeit a little thinner) that would be just as strong, but I'm digressing, when you go premium, go big, go really big! And these are that.

Unfortunately the listing is kind of messed up and ambiguous. When I received them, as I hoped these are the stakes that are 8mm in diameter and 300mm in length. They are also around 70 grams a piece, not the lighter weight which my understanding is for a shorter version. I was anticipating the extra weight since another reviewer gave meaningful and helpful feedback. I completely understand and agree with the criticisms expressed about the heavy weight and the high cost. I also don't think these are good for backpacking, possibly could work for staking down heavier things like EzUps or large canopies. These are SOLID and reflect that fact with heavy weight. I don't mind that they weigh a lot because I only plan to use two of these stakes for setting up a secure ridgeline across poles, with lighter weight stakes for the guylines.

The cordage loops at the end seem kind of cheap and low quality in comparison to the stakes themselves. The stake materials, welds and finishing all look great, although a couple stakes new-out-of-the-package have a slight curve/bend to them. There are no sharp edges or other apparent issues. Overall I'm very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: TiTo High Strength Titanium Alloy Tent Stakes Tent pegs Nail pegs for Canopy Camping Tent Dia 8mm and Length 240mm only 56G (8x300mm)
